reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes joining Forsage TRON through an Eagle/Forsage team and contacting a link provider to enter a level-based matrix system. It presents repeat slot purchases, TRX or dollar payments, escalating claimed gains, and short-period earning examples, then urges viewers to join without delay. Anti-scam reassurances and inconsistent money-flow statements are also present but do not remove the video's direct promotion of the earning system.

citations.quote: So here in this system we market based from Matrix Which in Forsage design, both in Matrix These are X3 and X4
if you join my team, you will save profits as well
If you want to join the system then the person who given you the link you can call
if the position is filled then you will get the profit

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker does not ask viewers to trust every approach made in the video's name. He explicitly warns that commenters offering a contact number to join are scammers, says viewers should not hand money to the company, and cautions against joining blindly. Those warnings matter when assessing whether this is a deceptive solicitation: the speaker identifies a concrete impersonation risk and tells viewers to think before participating. His discussion of earnings should be read alongside those cautions, not in isolation.

citations.quote: If anybody in the comment box gives you a contact number if you can join with us that person is a scammer
first thing is you don't give money to company
because of more people is joining the system blindly so I request to them to not do it

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution points to the matrix and the invitation to contact the person who supplied the link. Neither quote by itself establishes that the speaker wants viewers to pay an impersonator or to join without scrutiny. The narrower contact instruction is consistent with his warning about unsolicited commenters, while his express objection to blind joining complicates the claim that this is an unqualified recruitment pitch.

citations.quote: If anybody in the comment box gives you a contact number if you can join with us that person is a scammer
because of more people is joining the system blindly so I request to them to not do it

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The warning distinguishes approved contacts from commenters; it does not warn viewers away from the system. The speaker directs interested viewers to the person who gave them the link, urges them to join without delay, and describes profit from filled positions. Those are affirmative recruitment and earning claims despite the caution about blind joining.

citations.quote: If you want to join the system then the person who given you the link you can call
join without delay
if the position is filled then you will get the profit

opening.argument: Judge, much of the presentation teaches an operating model rather than simply demanding a payment. The speaker says he will explain how the system works, identifies X3 and X4 as the two matrices, and breaks out their positions and level-dependent amounts. Even the earnings discussion is tied to how levels work. An explanation of a mechanism can include examples and participation instructions without every description of possible profit being a verified promise of a particular outcome.

citations.quote: In this video i will guide you on the method how can you generate money from Foursat & how did the system work
in X3 matrix there are three positions and in X4 there are total six positions
Profit rate depends on your level

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's matrix quote identifies the subject being explained, not the speaker's sole purpose. Likewise, 'if the position is filled' describes a condition for payment, not proof that payment is automatic or guaranteed for every viewer. The explanation of X3 and X4 positions supplies context the opening leaves out.

citations.quote: So here in this system we market based from Matrix Which in Forsage design, both in Matrix These are X3 and X4
if the position is filled then you will get the profit
in X3 matrix there are three positions and in X4 there are total six positions

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The operational detail explains the earning scheme being promoted; it does not make the video a detached tutorial. The speaker links joining his team to profit, presents filled positions as the route to payment, and closes by telling interested viewers to contact their link provider. The conditional wording does not remove that invitation.

citations.quote: if you join my team, you will save profits as well
if the position is filled then you will get the profit
If you want to join the system then the person who given you the link you can call

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker draws a distinction between this arrangement and paying a company for a promised multiple: he expressly denies that '$100 in, $200 out' is the transaction. He instead describes participants working with TRX, marketing through matrices, and receiving different amounts at different levels. The record does show team-based payments, so there is no reason to conceal that; the narrower point is that the cited material does not establish a guaranteed company payout or a request for account credentials. Those missing elements matter before treating the explanation of a commercial arrangement as proof of deception.

citations.quote: this is not the scheme that you give 100$ to the company and the company gives you a profit of 200$
So here the company's Main Mission that is that TRX has to increase users
So here in this system we market based from Matrix
Profit rate depends on your level

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's evidence supports an invitation into a level-based team, but an invitation alone does not show the particular company-deposit promise the speaker disavows. The filled-position quote also makes payment conditional. The judge should distinguish an asserted marketing arrangement from proof that the speaker has promised every entrant a fixed return.

citations.quote: This is not some thing like you pay 100 dollar and company gives you 200 dollar profit one day company ran away
if the position is filled then you will get the profit

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A fixed company payout or credential request is not necessary to identify the mechanism shown here. The speaker invites viewers into his team, ties profit to filled positions, and warns that failing to obtain the next level can mean missed profits. The X4 slide also depicts an upline and a repeat slot purchase. Denying one simple deposit-and-return story does not explain away recruitment-linked matrix payments.
